source.title: Linear Mode Connectivity under Data Shifts for Deep Ensembles of Image Classifiers
source.authors: Carol E. Hepburn; Tobias Zielke; A. Raulf

record.file_problem: The supplied text appears to contain the full paper and appendix; no truncation or document mismatch is evident.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures linear interpolation barriers and interpolated-model performance under data shifts. It does not test the claim versions about natural-label generalization gaps, random-label memorization, or the listed generalization mechanisms. Its generalization findings concern interpolation under shifted training subsets.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test-performance changes for linearly interpolated models, but these do not measure the training-versus-test generalization gap named in the claim versions. Its comments about sharp minima and generalization cite prior work and are not its own measurements.
record.test_reason: The study measures connectivity between trained solutions, interpolation performance under data shifts, and ensemble diversity. Batch-size comparisons concern interpolation barriers and accuracy relative to endpoint models, not held-out performance of large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets. It does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or its ranking of generalization gaps. Its convolutional versus MLP ensemble results do not establish the single-network architectural comparison in V3.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that data shifts can destabilize training trajectories, that larger batches or smaller learning rates can mitigate this instability, and that LMC-sampled models share errors more frequently than independently initialized models. Their proposed sharpness explanations are interpretations drawing on prior work, rather than measurements of magnitude-aware sharpness or its correlation with generalization gaps.
record.recipe_differences: The study examines linear connectivity, interpolation barriers and ensemble behavior under data shifts; it does not apply the original claim's random-label memorization or generalization-gap tests.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcomes vary with architecture and depth, data shift type and severity, batch size, learning rate, image normalization, and batch normalization.

fits_no_version.finding: Interpolated models can lose test performance under data shifts even when test-loss barriers are small or zero; normalization and batch normalization affect these outcomes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Small interpolation loss barriers need not imply preservation of endpoint-model test performance under data shifts.

fits_no_version.finding: Table III reports higher test accuracy for ensembles trained from different initializations than for LMC-sampled ensembles, accompanied by lower wrong agreement. Convolutional ensembles also outperform the MLP ensembles in these experiments.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Ensemble sampling strategy and architecture affect functional diversity and ensemble test accuracy.

record.problems: The evidence concerns interpolation barriers and interpolated-model performance rather than a direct train-test generalization gap. Some findings are described through figures; the supplied text does not give precise values for all figure results.
record.rows_left_out: Other interpolation conditions and architecture-specific results appear in Figures 4, 7, 11–16 and Appendix I, Tables VI–VIII. They were not extracted because they measure interpolation stability or loss barriers without directly testing a listed claim version; selected numerical and explicitly described test-performance results are represented above.

untested.parts: Joint demonstration of random-label fitting, chance-level random-label test accuracy, and natural-label generalization.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Single-network convolutional versus fully connected test-error comparison; contributions of local connectivity, learned sparsity, and convolutional initialization.
Held-out performance comparisons between adaptive optimizers and SGD under specified tuning budgets.
Large versus small batch held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and recovery through recipe changes.
Dropout's effect on held-out error. Dropout appears in experimental conditions, but interpolation differences do not isolate its effect on classifier test error.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance, its correlation with training-test gaps, and comparison with norm- and margin-based rankings.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The exclusion rests on the specific outcomes and comparisons measured, not on a requirement that every generalization claim involve a training-test gap. Table III's ensemble comparison falls outside V3's single-network claim. Other unrecorded interpolation conditions are already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label test accuracy.
Width beyond the interpolation threshold and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected test-error comparisons.
Large versus small batch test performance under a fixed epoch budget.
Magnitude-aware sharpness as a predictor of the training-test gap.
Effect of removing memorized examples on test accuracy.

rows.subject: MLP L3 W256-512-256
rows.operation_detail: Measured test accuracy difference for interpolation between models trained on equal CIFAR-10 subsets without batch normalization.
rows.measure: Test accuracy difference (∆) for interpolated models
rows.value: ∼ 16% performance drop on average despite zero barriers
rows.note: The reported quantity concerns interpolated models; it does not establish a training-test gap.
rows.check: The CIFAR-10 model is L3 W110-256-110, with 395,826 parameters and P/N 15.83, rather than the listed MNIST architecture. Table VI gives an accuracy difference of −16.22 ± 3.32 percentage points. The baseline is mean endpoint-model test accuracy.

rows.subject: ResNet 22
rows.operation_detail: Measured interpolated-model test performance after training copies on balanced versus imbalanced disjoint CIFAR-10 subsets.

conditions.value: different samples for the comparison described in Fig. 8

rows.locator: Section IV-E; Fig. 8; Appendix I, Table VII
rows.note: The measure is an interpolation accuracy difference, not train-test gap.
rows.check: The quoted Table VII values belong to ResNet10 on MNIST at learning rate 10−3, not ResNet22 on CIFAR-10. Its parameter count is 303,866 and P/N is 10.13. The balanced entry is not marked as using different SGD-noise samples; imbalance introduces different samples. Figure 8 illustrates a different comparison. Each accuracy difference is relative to its own endpoint-model mean.

rows.subject: VGG-like
rows.operation_detail: Measured test weighted-average-precision difference for interpolation between models trained on separate spectral bands or band combinations.

conditions.value: different single bands or band combinations

rows.value: Interpolated-model generalization worsens for single-band training, especially with larger domain shifts; up to 15% accuracy loss is reported in the figure caption
rows.note: The paper describes weighted average precision in the section; figure caption describes ∆ as a weighted-average-precision difference. This is under domain shift, not the claimed gap.
rows.check: Report the outcome as a weighted-average-precision difference relative to mean endpoint performance. The caption's approximate 15% loss should not be presented as classification accuracy or an established relative-percent decrease.

rows.subject: MLP L3 W256-512-256
rows.operation_detail: Compared interpolation barrier and accuracy difference for centered versus [0,1]-normalized CIFAR-10 data.
rows.locator: Section IV-G; Appendix I, Table VIII
rows.note: This compares data normalization effects on interpolation outcomes, not training-test gaps.
rows.check: The centered-data barrier is 1.01 ± 0.24, not 0.0 ± 0.0. The CIFAR-10 architecture is L3 W110-256-110, with 395,826 parameters and P/N 15.83. The other quoted Table VIII values match.

rows.subject: MLP L3 W256-512-256 Batch norm.
rows.operation_detail: Compared interpolation barrier and accuracy difference for centered versus [0,1]-normalized CIFAR-10 data with batch normalization.
rows.locator: Section IV-G; Appendix I, Table VIII
rows.note: The paper says batch normalization restores stability for the normalization comparison; these are interpolation measures, not the claim's gap.
rows.check: The CIFAR-10 architecture is L3 W110-256-110 with batch normalization, not W256-512-256. The stated parameter count and ratio describe the wrong base architecture. Table VIII's numerical outcomes match, but the nonzero barriers do not by themselves establish literal convergence to one minimum.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
